selected_passages.title: raw:sources/News_publisher_files_class_action_antitrust_suit_against_Google_citing_AI_s_harms_to_their_bottom_line
selected_passages.text: A new class action lawsuit filed this week in the U.S. District Court in D.C. accuses Google and parent company Alphabet of anticompetitive behavior in violation of U.S. antitrust law, the Sherman Act, and others, on behalf of news publishers. The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means. It also specifically cites new AI technologies like Google’s Search Generative Experience (SGE) and Bard AI chatbot as worsening the problem.

selected_passages.title: sources/Is_Google_Search_better_than_the_rest_And_is_that_fair
selected_passages.text:
- Google's extensive data collection on searches and interactions is a primary advantage for personalization but a point of contention for privacy advocates.
- Legal challenges to Google's default status face hurdles because users often actively choose Google over other providers despite initial defaults.
- Allegations exist that Google manipulates search queries to maximize ad revenue, though Google denies altering organic results.
- The volume of indexed data has grown exponentially from 9 ZB in 2013 to over 120 ZB in 2023, changing the nature of search results.
- Google utilizes machine learning and semantic matching to refine queries, while critics argue this widens the content pool to favor monetization.
